recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中一大片淡粉紅色、界線不清的上皮樣組織球聚集（非乾酪性肉芽腫），插圖可見多核巨細胞（箭頭）；抗酸染色下組織球內滿是洋紅色成團的桿菌（箭頭），符合瀰漫性鳥型分枝桿菌複合群（MAC）感染。
features: Large, poorly formed aggregate of pale eosinophilic epithelioid histiocytes replacing marrow
No caseous necrosis within the granulomatous area
Inset: histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells (arrows)
Acid-fast stain: numerous magenta-staining bacilli packed within histiocyte cytoplasm, forming clusters (arrows)
Residual hematopoietic marrow and fat surrounding the lesion
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine shows a large, ill-defined, noncaseating granulomatous aggregate composed of sheets of pale epithelioid histiocytes that replaces a substantial portion of the intertrabecular space, with multinucleated giant cells seen at higher power; residual hematopoiesis and fat surround the lesion. The acid-fast stain demonstrates abundant magenta acid-fast bacilli clustered within histiocytes. Findings are consistent with disseminated mycobacterial infection with marrow granulomas, compatible with Mycobacterium avium complex in the appropriate clinical setting; culture or molecular identification is required for speciation.

ddx.vs: TB granulomas are usually well formed with caseous necrosis and few bacilli, whereas MAC in immunocompromised hosts forms loose histiocytic sheets packed with bacilli; culture/PCR is definitive.
Histoplasma yeasts are small intracellular organisms that are GMS/PAS positive and not acid-fast.
Sarcoid granulomas are tight, well formed and lack organisms on AFB and fungal stains.
Granulomas accompany CD30+/CD15+ Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells and no acid-fast organisms are seen.
